title: Greece Faces Twin Test: Climate Shocks Strain Budgets · 25 Aug
keywords: Greece, wildfires, heatwaves, climate risk, fiscal policy, public debt, inflation, cost of living, European Union, tax cuts, tourism, Bank of Greece, Eurostat, debt reduction, economic recovery
notes: Greece is confronting a paradox at the heart of its recovery story: public debt is falling faster than expected, yet repeated wildfires and stubborn cost-of-living pressures are eroding public confidence in that progress. Senior advisers now regard climate-driven disruption as a medium- to long-term fiscal risk, complicating Athens' efforts to turn economic improvement into political capital. The country is increasingly seen across the European Union as a test case for whether a heavily indebted member state can absorb climate shocks and maintain fiscal discipline while still delivering tangible relief to ordinary households.
